## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-sparse`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-sparse)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-sparse`:

$$
2^{O(k/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(k(\log\log k)^2/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Let m = |E(G)|. Handle edgeless graphs directly. Return NO if m > (2Δ−1)k; otherwise keep the graph and remove isolated vertices.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O_\Delta(k)$ |
| Clauses | $O_\Delta(k)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $3$ |

## Derivation

1. One selected edge uv dominates at most deg(u)+deg(v)−1 ≤ 2Δ−1 edges, including itself. Hence every YES instance satisfies m ≤ (2Δ−1)k. After the rejection rule, m = O_Δ(k) and there are at most 2m nonisolated vertices.

2. Use one choice bit x_e per remaining edge. For each vertex compute $z_v\leftrightarrow\bigvee_{e\ni v}x_e$ by shared binary OR gates with full equivalences. For each edge uv add $z_u\vee z_v$. These conditions exactly express edge domination.

3. Add $\sum_e x_e\le k$ with the linear cardinality circuit. The [general-m encoding](exact-edge-dominating-set.md) has O(m) variables and clauses, so here N+M = O_Δ(k) and w ≤ 3.

4. Apply the sparse SAT assumption, using forced-zero density padding if necessary. The preprocessing and encoding are polynomial-time and decision-preserving; the resulting bound is B(k)L^{O(1)}, with constants depending on fixed Δ.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- Δ must be fixed independently of k and of the input. The displayed constants do not provide the same bound for unrestricted maximum degree.
- The budget is the number of selected edges. Without the maximum-degree restriction, one selected edge can dominate arbitrarily many edges and the rejection rule gives no O(k) edge bound.
- This is a direct size-reduction and encoding argument, not a claim that the ordinary Vertex Cover kernel preserves Edge Dominating Set.

A decision-preserving kernel does not automatically preserve the number of solutions.
